findings.title: Cache status ignores the calendar-cache feature flag and in-memory delegation credentials
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when caching is disabled. It then queries `calendarCache.groupBy` with `credentialId IN (...)`. `connectedCalendars` can include in-memory delegation credentials with negative ids; these ids are passed straight to the query. The mock added in this PR (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returning `[]`) is never reachable from here.

findings.title: Ownership check only matches credentials with credential.userId, excluding team/delegation credentials
findings.body: The credential lookup filters on `userId: user.id` only, so credentials the user can legitimately see but which are not directly owned (for example, team credentials) cannot have their cache deleted. The UI still shows the delete option for those credentials, so the user gets a generic error. Failure is also signalled with a plain `Error`, which tRPC maps to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of a `TRPCError` with NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.

findings.title: Extra unconditional DB write bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt on every cache refresh
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs an UPDATE across all selected calendars for the credential after every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. Prisma's `@updatedAt` will bump the column. This is a write amplification on a hot webhook path, with locking across every row of the credential. Nothing in the UI uses it (the PR notes admit the frontend uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`). The `{}` payload is also fragile and unclear. This should be removed.

findings.title: Cache actions show only for Google credentials; Cache Status item is a focusable menu item
findings.body: `hasCache` is `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`, which has type `false | Date | null | undefined`. The 'Cache Status' entry is rendered as a `DropdownMenuItem`, so it is interactive/focusable and closes the menu on select even though it is purely informational. The date is formatted with a hard-coded `en-US` locale, ignoring the user's locale. `Intl.DateTimeFormat` also formats in the browser timezone without regard to the user's profile timezone.

findings.title: Delete-cache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: On success the delete-cache mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` (which is `props.onChanged`, possibly undefined). It does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` as the disconnect mutation does. After deletion the UI continues to show a stale 'Last updated' timestamp and the delete option until a manual refetch (`refetchOnWindowFocus` is false).

findings.title: Unrelated dev script is macOS-only and has bugs
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU/Linux. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script. The script is unrelated to the PR's stated feature. Alongside the unrelated `dev:cron` change to `npx tsx` (which is not a declared dependency), this should be split out of the PR.

findings.title: Migration header comment contradicts the statement
findings.body: The auto-generated warning says the column is added 'without a default value', but the statement adds `DEFAULT NOW()`. All existing cache rows get the migration timestamp as `updatedAt`, so the UI will show a misleading 'last updated' time for rows that were refreshed long ago.
